title: Saying More Than One Noun
goal: Form and recognize common Norwegian noun plurals in indefinite and definite forms.

objectives.statement: Form and recognize common Norwegian noun plurals in indefinite and definite forms.

sections.title: Getting ready for the neighborhood meeting

spans.value: Nora and Amir are preparing a room for a neighborhood meeting. Nora checks the room while Amir brings things in from the hall.
Det står fire stoler i gangen.

blocks.translation: There are four chairs in the hall.

spans.value: Fint. Kan du sette stolene ved bordene?

blocks.translation: Good. Can you put the chairs by the tables?
Yes. Where should the cups go?

spans.value: Sett koppene på bordet, og legg eplene i skålen.

blocks.translation: Put the cups on the table, and put the apples in the bowl.
Yes, the glasses are in the kitchen.

spans.value: The conversation distinguishes between things mentioned as a quantity and things treated as a known group. Amir first says that there are
, “four chairs.” Nora then calls the same chairs
, “the chairs,” because both speakers now know which chairs she means.
This chapter focuses on making and recognizing those two plural forms.

sections.title: Some common nouns change inside the word

spans.value: Not every frequent noun follows the regular patterns. Some change a vowel or have another irregular plural form. These forms need to be learned with the noun.
Compare singular, indefinite plural, and definite plural:
Use the complete plural form rather than adding a regular ending to the singular:

en.value: There are books on the table.
Two men are carrying a table.
The men put the table by the door.

sections.title: Following a noun through a conversation

spans.value: A natural conversation often introduces a group with an indefinite plural and then refers back to it with a definite plural:

no.value: Nora kjøper epler. Eplene ligger i en pose.

en.value: Nora buys apples. The apples are in a bag.

spans.value: The first sentence introduces some apples. The second sentence refers to those same apples.

no.value: Amir finner tre kopper. Koppene står på kjøkkenet.

en.value: Amir finds three cups. The cups are in the kitchen.

no.value: Det står to bord i gangen. Bordene er tunge.

en.value: There are two tables in the hall. The tables are heavy.

spans.value: This movement from indefinite to definite explains the forms in the opening dialogue:

no.value: Det står fire stoler i gangen.

en.value: There are four chairs in the hall.

no.value: Kan du sette stolene ved bordene?

en.value: Can you put the chairs by the tables?

spans.value: Once the chairs have been introduced,
also refers to particular tables that Nora and Amir can identify in the room.

Do not choose the definite plural merely because a noun appears for the second time mechanically. Choose it because the speakers can identify the intended group from earlier words or from the shared situation.

sections.title: Cumulative transfer: preparing for a picnic

spans.value: Now change the situation. Instead of preparing a meeting room, imagine that a family is packing for a picnic. They need bags, cups, apples, books for the children, and several glasses or reusable drinking cups. Some objects are mentioned for the first time; others are already packed and can be identified.

Without returning to the tables above, write the indefinite and definite plural forms of several familiar nouns from the chapter. Then complete a short two-sentence scene in which the first sentence introduces more than one object and the second refers back to the same objects.
Your review should show two things: you can form common plural nouns, and you can choose between “some objects” and “the identifiable objects” in context.
